study_identification.title: Multivariate brain-cognition associations in euthymic bipolar disorder

study_characteristics.study_objective: Assess multivariate associations between cortical thickness abnormalities and cognitive performance (processing speed, attention, executive function) in euthymic bipolar disorder using normative modeling and canonical correlation analysis.

dataset_name.answer: HCP Young Adult; OpenBHB; OASIS-3; Cam-CAN; Newcastle University healthy adults (NCL); BLISS local healthy controls included for harmonization
dataset_name.reason: The normative model used large public healthy control datasets (HCP, OpenBHB, OASIS-3, Cam-CAN) and an additional Newcastle University healthy cohort; BLISS local HCs (n=26) were included during harmonization to estimate site offset.
dataset_name.supporting_text: We utilised four public datasets of T1-weighted scans from healthy controls... HCP; OpenBHB; OASIS-3; Cam-CAN... We also used a cohort of healthy adult participants scanned at Newcastle University (NCL). We harmonised the normative-HC data, including the 26 HCs recruited to BLISS...

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Group comparisons via t-tests/Mann–Whitney and chi-squared for demographics; FDR-controlled ROI-wise CT differences. Canonical correlation analysis (CCA) between z-scored cognitive variables and cortical thickness PCs (23 PCs explaining 90%). First canonical correlation r=0.860, Pillai's Trace p=0.112; permutation p=0.093. DSST and TMT-B loaded most; key regions: left inferior temporal (rho=0.406, p=0.002), right entorhinal (rho=0.380, p=0.004), right temporal pole (rho=0.334, p=0.012).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: BD showed deficits in processing speed, attention, and executive function and exhibited abnormal cortical thickness; multivariate associations linked PS/EF performance to temporal cortical regions, though the primary CCA correlation did not reach significance.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Compared to HCs, BD had significant impairments on several cognitive tests and abnormalities in CT across regions (FDR-controlled). CCA using 7 cognitive variables and 23 CT PCs yielded a strongest canonical correlation of 0.860 (Pillai's Trace p=0.112; permutation p=0.093). DSST and TMT-B contributed most to the canonical variate; regions most associated with the cognitive variate were left inferior temporal (rho=0.406, p=0.002), right entorhinal (rho=0.380, p=0.004), and right temporal pole (rho=0.334, p=0.012); additional significant but subthreshold loadings included right inferior temporal (rho=0.286, p=0.032), right pars orbitalis (rho=0.268, p=0.046), and right superior temporal (rho=0.297, p=0.026).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Modest sample size limits power; primary CCA association did not achieve statistical significance; cross-sectional design; no education adjustment in cognitive residualization (by design); normative model validation metrics (e.g., calibration, out-of-sample performance) not reported; analysis limited to ROI-level cortical thickness (single modality).
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Demonstrates leveraging multi-site public datasets to build a normative model and adjust site effects via GAM; integrates ROI-level normative z-scores with multivariate CCA; manual QC and FLAIR-assisted pial refinement to improve CT reliability.

general_notes.general_notes: Supplement Table S1 details normative-HC composition: CamCAN (n=644), OASIS-3 (n=542), OpenBHB (n=3984), HCP (n=1113), NCL (n=61); overall mean age 32.64, 50.3% female. Outlier removal excluded 393 controls (>5 MAD residuals). PCA reduced CT to 23 PCs explaining 90% variance before CCA. Cognitive data were imputed (5% missing), age and premorbid IQ regressed out in HCs, and standardized; some variables transformed to achieve multivariate normality (see supplement).
